jp: 雨[あめ]{が|ga-subject}降[ふ]っ{たら|tara-conditional}、家[いえ]{で|de-place}本[ほん]{を|o-object}読[よ]みます。
en: If it rains, I'll read a book at home.
why: A plain 'if' with a free main clause takes たら, which attaches to the past stem (降った).

jp: 駅[えき]{に|ni-destination}着[つ]い{たら|tara-conditional}、電話[でんわ]します。
en: When I get to the station, I'll call you.
why: 'Once A is done, I'll do B' with a deliberate action in the main clause takes たら.

jp: 時間[じかん]{が|ga-existence}あっ{たら|tara-conditional}、映画[えいが]{を|o-object}見[み]{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きませんか。
en: If you have time, would you like to go and see a movie?
why: An invitation in the main clause fits たら; ても would mean 'even if you have time'.

jp: 明日[あした]天気[てんき]{が|ga-subject}よかっ{たら|tara-conditional}、海[うみ]{へ/に|e-direction}出[で]かけます。
en: If the weather is nice tomorrow, I'll head out to the sea.
why: The main clause states what I will do, and たら hangs on the past stem よかっ.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]{が|ga-subject}終[お]わっ{たら|tara-conditional}、ゲーム{を|o-object}します。
en: When my homework is finished, I'll play a game.
why: Completion of one event before a planned action is the core job of たら.

jp: 疲[つか]れ{たら|tara-conditional}、少[すこ]し休[やす]みましょう。
en: If you get tired, let's rest for a bit.
why: たら is the natural link from 'if/when X happens' to a suggestion with ましょう; と can never lead into one.

jp: 日本[にほん]{へ/に|ni-destination}来[き]{たら|tara-conditional}、ぜひ連絡[れんらく]{を|o-object}ください。
en: If you come to Japan, please be sure to contact me.
why: A request in the main clause calls for たら; ても would mean 'even if you come'.

jp: 夏休[なつやす]み{に|ni-change}なっ{たら|tara-conditional}、友[とも]だち{と|to-with}旅行[りょこう]します。
en: When summer vacation comes, I'll travel with friends.
why: A planned action after a point in time is reached takes たら on the past stem なっ.

jp: お金[かね]{が|ga-existence}たくさんあっ{たら|tara-conditional}、大[おお]きい家[いえ]{を|o-object}買[か]いたいです。
en: If I had a lot of money, I would want to buy a big house.
why: A wish (たい) in the main clause pairs with たら, not with と.

jp: 道[みち]{が|ga-stative}わからなかっ{たら|tara-conditional}、あの人[ひと]{に|ni-target}聞[き]きます。
en: If I don't know the way, I'll ask that person.
why: A negative 'if' uses the past negative stem わからなかっ plus たら.

jp: 明日[あした]{が|ga-subject}休[やす]みだっ{たら|tara-conditional}、友[とも]だち{と|to-with}遊[あそ]びます。
en: If tomorrow is a day off, I'll play with my friends.
why: After a noun, たら attaches to だった (休みだったら), and the main clause can state a plan.

jp: この店[みせ]{の|no-possessive}パン{が|ga-subject}安[やす]かっ{たら|tara-conditional}、たくさん食[た]べます。
en: If the bread at this shop is cheap, I'll eat a lot of it.
why: For an i-adjective, たら attaches to the past stem 安かっ.

jp: ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}食[た]べ{たら|tara-conditional}、すぐ歯[は]{を|o-object}みがきます。
en: After I eat, I brush my teeth right away.
why: 'After A is done, B' with a habit or plan takes たら on the past stem 食べ.

jp: 寒[さむ]かっ{たら|tara-conditional}、窓[まど]{を|o-object}閉[し]めましょう{か|ka-question}。
en: If you're cold, shall I close the window?
why: An offer with ましょうか follows a たら clause naturally; と cannot lead into an offer, and ば would need the form 寒ければ.

jp: 試験[しけん]{に|ni-target}合格[ごうかく]し{たら|tara-conditional}、ケーキ{を|o-object}作[つく]ります。
en: If I pass the exam, I'll bake a cake.
why: A hoped-for result followed by my own planned action takes たら.

jp: 大[おお]きくなっ{たら|tara-conditional}、医者[いしゃ]{に|ni-change}なりたいです。
en: When I grow up, I want to become a doctor.
why: A wish about the future after growing up takes たら on the past stem 大きくなっ.

jp: もし明日[あした]暑[あつ]かっ{たら|tara-conditional}、プール{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きましょう。
en: If it's hot tomorrow, let's go to the pool.
why: The past stem 暑かっ takes たら; with もし and a suggestion (ましょう), たら is the everyday choice and と is impossible.

jp: 分[わ]からない言葉[ことば]{が|ga-existence}あっ{たら|tara-conditional}、辞書[じしょ]{で|de-means}調[しら]べなさい。
en: If there's a word you don't understand, look it up in a dictionary.
why: The past stem あっ takes たら, the usual 'if' before a command (なさい); と can never introduce a command.

jp: 家[いえ]{に/へ|ni-destination}帰[かえ]っ{たら|tara-conditional}、まず手[て]{を|o-object}洗[あら]います。
en: When I get home, I first wash my hands.
why: The first action after arriving home is described with たら on the past stem 帰っ.

jp: 少[すこ]し休[やす]ん{だら|tara-conditional}どうですか。
en: Why don't you rest for a little while?
why: A suggestion 'how about doing X' is made with たら (voiced だら after ん) plus どうですか.

jp: どうし{たら|tara-conditional}いいですか。
en: What should I do?
why: 'What should I do?' is the fixed pattern どうしたらいいですか, built on たら.

jp: どこ{で|de-place}切符[きっぷ]{を|o-object}買[か]っ{たら|tara-conditional}いいですか。
en: Where should I buy a ticket?
why: 'Where should I do X' uses the fixed pattern 〜たらいいですか on the past stem 買っ.

jp: 窓[まど]{を|o-object}開[あ]け{たら|tara-conditional}、外[そと]{は|wa-topic}雪[ゆき]でした。
en: When I opened the window, it was snowing outside.
why: A discovery after a completed action ('I did A and found B') uses たら.

jp: 朝[あさ]起[お]き{たら|tara-conditional}、もう十時[じゅうじ]でした。
en: When I woke up in the morning, it was already ten o'clock.
why: Finding something surprising after waking up is a past discovery, which takes たら.

jp: 外[そと]{に/へ|ni-destination}出[で]{たら|tara-conditional}、雨[あめ]{が|ga-subject}降[ふ]っていました。
en: When I went outside, it was raining.
why: A past discovery ('I went out and found it raining') is a たら sentence, attached to the stem 出.

jp: 検査[けんさ]{を|o-object}受[う]け{たら|tara-conditional}、問題[もんだい]{は/が|wa-negative}ありませんでした。
en: When I had the check-up, there turned out to be no problem.
why: A result found after a completed event in the past is expressed with たら.

jp: 辞書[じしょ]{を|o-object}引[ひ]い{たら|tara-conditional}、すぐ意味[いみ]{が|ga-stative}わかりました。
en: When I looked it up in a dictionary, I understood the meaning right away.
why: After a completed action, a past result is reported with たら on the past stem 引い.

jp: 大学[だいがく]{を|o-departure}卒業[そつぎょう]し{たら|tara-conditional}、すぐ働[はたら]くつもりです。
en: Once I graduate from university, I plan to start working right away.
why: An intention (つもり) in the main clause means たら is needed; と and ば cannot lead into it.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}お酒[さけ]{を|o-object}飲[の]ん{だら|tara-conditional}、すぐ顔[かお]{が|ga-subject}赤[あか]くなります。
en: When my brother drinks alcohol, his face turns red right away.
why: Voiced だら follows a past stem ending in ん, as in 飲んだら.

jp: ベル{が|ga-subject}鳴[な]っ{たら|tara-conditional}、鉛筆[えんぴつ]{を|o-object}置[お]いてください。
en: When the bell rings, please put down your pencil.
why: A request after an expected event takes たら on the past stem 鳴っ; ても would mean 'even if the bell rings'.

jp: 宝[たから]くじ{に|ni-target}当[あ]たっ{たら|tara-conditional}、世界[せかい]{を|o-path}旅行[りょこう]したいです。
en: If I won the lottery, I'd like to travel around the world.
why: A dream 'if X happened, I'd want Y' is a typical たら sentence.

jp: 傘[かさ]{を|o-object}忘[わす]れ{たら|tara-conditional}、駅[えき]{で|de-place}買[か]います。
en: If I forget my umbrella, I'll buy one at the station.
why: A plan for what I will do in a possible situation takes たら.

jp: 天気[てんき]{が|ga-subject}悪[わる]かっ{たら|tara-conditional}、試合[しあい]{は|wa-topic}中止[ちゅうし]{に|ni-change}なります。
en: If the weather is bad, the game will be cancelled.
why: The past stem 悪かっ plus たら states the condition; ても would mean 'even if the weather is bad'.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]{が|ga-subject}終[お]わっ{たら|tara-conditional}、すぐお知[し]らせします。
en: As soon as the meeting is over, I'll let you know.
why: A promise to act after something finishes takes たら on the past stem 終わっ.

jp: 京都[きょうと]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]っ{たら|tara-conditional}、古[ふる]いお寺[てら]{を|o-object}見[み]たいです。
en: When I go to Kyoto, I want to see old temples.
why: A wish (たい) about what to do once there takes たら on the past stem 行っ; ても would mean 'even if I go'.

jp: 日本語[にほんご]{が|potential-ga}上手[じょうず]に話[はな]せ{たら|tara-conditional}いい{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: It would be nice if I could speak Japanese well.
why: The pattern 〜たらいい expresses a wish ('it would be nice if...').

jp: 毎日[まいにち]運動[うんどう]し{たら|tara-conditional}、元気[げんき]{に|ni-change}なるでしょう。
en: If you exercise every day, you will become healthy.
why: A prediction after an assumed action takes たら attached to し (the past stem of する).

jp: 雪[ゆき]{が|ga-subject}たくさん積[つ]もっ{たら|tara-conditional}、雪[ゆき]だるま{を|o-object}作[つく]りましょう。
en: If a lot of snow piles up, let's make a snowman.
why: A proposal (ましょう) in the main clause requires たら.

jp: 具合[ぐあい]{が|ga-subject}悪[わる]かっ{たら|tara-conditional}、すぐ病院[びょういん]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きなさい。
en: If you feel unwell, go to the hospital right away.
why: The past stem 悪かっ takes たら, the usual 'if' before a command; と can never introduce a command.

jp: スープ{が|ga-subject}冷[さ]め{たら|tara-conditional}、おいしくなくなります。
en: If the soup gets cold, it stops tasting good.
why: Past-stem 冷め plus たら gives the plain 'if the soup cools' condition.

jp: 郵便局[ゆうびんきょく]{が|ga-subject}開[あ]い{たら|tara-conditional}、この手紙[てがみ]{を|o-object}出[だ]します。
en: When the post office opens, I'll send this letter.
why: A planned action once an event happens takes たら on the past stem 開い.

jp: 料理[りょうり]{が|ga-subject}でき{たら|tara-conditional}、みんな{を|o-object}呼[よ]びます。
en: When the food is ready, I'll call everyone.
why: 'When X is ready, I'll do Y' is the plain, deliberate-action use of たら.

jp: 手紙[てがみ]{を|o-object}書[か]い{たら|tara-conditional}、先生[せんせい]{に|ni-recipient}見[み]せます。
en: After I write the letter, I'll show it to my teacher.
why: A planned next step after finishing the first one takes たら.

jp: この薬[くすり]{を|o-object}飲[の]ん{だら|tara-conditional}、すぐよくなります。
en: If you take this medicine, you'll get better soon.
why: A voiced だら follows the past stem 飲ん; でも would mean 'even if you take it'.

jp: 電車[でんしゃ]{に|ni-target}乗[の]り遅[おく]れ{たら|tara-conditional}、タクシー{を|o-object}使[つか]います。
en: If I miss the train, I'll take a taxi.
why: A backup plan stated with a volitional main clause takes たら.

jp: 財布[さいふ]{を|o-object}拾[ひろ]っ{たら|tara-conditional}、交番[こうばん]{に|ni-destination}届[とど]けましょう。
en: If you find a wallet, let's take it to the police box.
why: A proposal with ましょう in the main clause calls for たら.

jp: 大人[おとな]{に|ni-change}なっ{たら|tara-conditional}、世界[せかい]{を|o-object}見[み]たいです。
en: When I become an adult, I want to see the world.
why: A wish about the future once a state is reached takes たら.

jp: 明日[あした]雨[あめ]じゃなかっ{たら|tara-conditional}、公園[こうえん]{で|de-place}遊[あそ]びましょう。
en: If it isn't raining tomorrow, let's play in the park.
why: After a negated noun (雨じゃない), たら attaches to the past stem じゃなかっ; と cannot lead into a suggestion.

jp: 電話[でんわ]{が|ga-existence}なかっ{たら|tara-conditional}、こちら{から|kara-from}かけます。
en: If I don't hear from you, I'll call you myself.
why: The negative past stem なかっ plus たら gives 'if there is none', and the main clause is my own action.

jp: バス{が|ga-subject}来[こ]なかっ{たら|tara-conditional}、歩[ある]きましょう。
en: If the bus doesn't come, let's walk.
why: A negative condition followed by a proposal takes たら on 来なかっ.

jp: お金[かね]{が|ga-existence}なかっ{たら|tara-conditional}、友[とも]だち{に/から|ni-source}借[か]ります。
en: If I don't have money, I'll borrow some from a friend.
why: The main clause states what I will do, which suits たら.

jp: この漢字[かんじ]{を|o-object}覚[おぼ]え{たら|tara-conditional}、テスト{は|wa-topic}大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]です。
en: Once you've memorized these kanji, the test will be fine.
why: 'Once A is done, B is fine' uses たら on the completed action 覚えた.

jp: 窓[まど]{を|o-object}閉[し]め{たら|tara-conditional}、部屋[へや]{が|ga-subject}静[しず]か{に|ni-change}なりました。
en: When I closed the window, the room became quiet.
why: A past discovery or result after a completed action is expressed with たら.

jp: ボタン{を|o-object}押[お]し{たら|tara-conditional}、ドア{が|ga-subject}開[あ]きました。
en: When I pressed the button, the door opened.
why: A past one-time result ('pressed it, and the door opened') takes たら.

jp: 名前[なまえ]{を|o-object}呼[よ]ん{だら|tara-conditional}、母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}驚[おどろ]きました。
en: When I called her name, my mother was surprised.
why: A one-time past event followed by a reaction uses たら (voiced だら after ん).

jp: あの店[みせ]{に|ni-destination}入[はい]っ{たら|tara-conditional}、先生[せんせい]{が|ga-existence}いました。
en: When I went into that shop, my teacher was there.
why: An unexpected discovery after entering is a past event, so it takes たら.

jp: 一週間[いっしゅうかん]{の|no-possessive}休[やす]み{が|potential-ga}もらえ{たら|tara-conditional}、沖縄[おきなわ]{で|de-place}ゆっくりしたいです。
en: If I could get a week off, I'd like to relax in Okinawa.
why: A wish about an imagined situation in the main clause calls for たら.

jp: この道[みち]{を|o-path}まっすぐ歩[ある]い{たら|tara-conditional}、右[みぎ]{に|ni-location}銀行[ぎんこう]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: If you walk straight along this road, there's a bank on your right.
why: A direction-giving 'if you do A you'll find B' takes たら on the past stem 歩い.

jp: ご飯[はん]{が|ga-subject}足[た]りなかっ{たら|tara-conditional}、パン{も|mo-also}あります。
en: If the rice isn't enough, there's bread too.
why: A negative condition 'if it isn't enough' takes たら on 足りなかっ.

jp: もし鳥[とり]だっ{たら|tara-conditional}、空[そら]{を|o-path}飛[と]びたいです。
en: If I were a bird, I'd want to fly through the sky.
why: A contrary-to-fact 'if I were X' with a wish in the main clause takes たら.

jp: 魔法[まほう]{が|potential-ga}使[つか]え{たら|tara-conditional}、何[なに]{を/が|o-object}したいです{か|ka-question}。
en: If you could use magic, what would you want to do?
why: A hypothetical question about wishes takes たら on the potential stem 使え.

jp: 五時[ごじ]{に|ni-change}なっ{たら|tara-conditional}、帰[かえ]ります。
en: When it becomes five o'clock, I'll go home.
why: A decision to act once a time arrives takes たら on the past stem なっ.

jp: 春[はる]{に|ni-change}なっ{たら|tara-conditional}、公園[こうえん]{で|de-place}花見[はなみ]{を|o-object}しましょう。
en: When spring comes, let's have a cherry-blossom picnic in the park.
why: An invitation once a season arrives takes たら on the past stem なっ; と cannot lead into an invitation.

jp: 電気[でんき]{を|o-object}消[け]し{たら|tara-conditional}、星[ほし]{が|potential-ga}よく見[み]えました。
en: When I turned off the light, I could see the stars clearly.
why: Something noticed right after a completed past action is expressed with たら on the stem 消し.

jp: うそ{を|o-object}つい{たら|tara-conditional}、先生[せんせい]{は/が|wa-topic}怒[おこ]るでしょう。
en: If you tell a lie, the teacher will probably be angry.
why: A conditional prediction with でしょう is a plain 'if' sentence marked by たら.

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]走[はし]っ{たら|tara-conditional}、体[からだ]{が|ga-subject}軽[かる]くなりました。
en: When I started running every morning, my body became lighter.
why: A result noticed after trying something is marked with たら on the past stem 走っ.

jp: ちょっと待[ま]っ{たら|tara-conditional}、バス{が|ga-subject}来[き]ました。
en: When I waited a little, the bus came.
why: A past 'I did A and then B happened' sequence is a たら sentence.

jp: あの車[くるま]{が|ga-subject}もう少[すこ]し安[やす]かっ{たら|tara-conditional}、すぐ決[き]めます。
en: If that car were a little cheaper, I'd decide right away.
why: The main clause states my own decision, so the condition takes たら.

jp: 雨[あめ]{が|ga-subject}止[や]ん{だら|tara-conditional}、洗濯物[せんたくもの]{を|o-object}外[そと]{に/で|ni-location}干[ほ]します。
en: When the rain stops, I'll hang the laundry outside.
why: A planned action once an event ends takes たら (voiced だら after ん in 止んだら).

jp: 風邪[かぜ]{を|o-object}ひい{たら|tara-conditional}、会社[かいしゃ]{を|o-object}休[やす]みます。
en: If I catch a cold, I'll take time off from work.
why: A plan for a possible situation takes たら attached to the past stem ひい.
